questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've heard that Melbourne was a great city to live in, and I felt that this would be a perfect opportunity to experience a place so far away from home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It is stressfull of course, but the university was very helpful in settling in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Melbourne Universitys "Stop 1" is a perfect place to get any assistance you might need. No matter what the problem is, you can go there and they will either directly help you or quickly send you to someone who can.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation was decent enough, but the events were a bit bland. Even though a lot of people didn't attend, I did meet a few friends here which held throughout the semester. The orientation itself was a single lecture in an auditorium. It was informative though.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The facebook group Fairy Floss Real Estate!!!! Some people go together in AirBnB's, but that's a "safe" option. The AirBnB's are often more expensive, and it is often very difficult to befriend locals, so for many, living in share houses is the only way to get to do this.
If you try to get a sharehouse like me, be aware that you have to spend quite a lot of energy in arranging meetings and such. I was lucky that I found a sharehouse that I could move into just after arriving, but I know other people who weren't as lucky, and lived in hostels for a week or two. If you have the money, university offerings are also pretty good, but they are so incredibly expensive that I could actually not believe it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You have to reach out more, as you aren't constantly surrounded by exchange students who wants to travel and socialise as much as you do. Instead, you get the chance to get some really good local friends in a cheaper, often spacious setting. Be aware that some of the older sharehouses don't use heating a lot as the houses are extremely poorly insulated, so the winters can be quite cold. 
It's also a perfect way to save huge amounts of money.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to get your student card, attend an orientation day, and otherwise it's all handled before you leave on their website. It can seem a bit stressfull with the formulas, but my feeling is that it matters way less than you might think.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email support, in-person support and a hotline.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got exactly the classes I signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry about it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think I had very high expectations based on their university rating, but in my experience, the arts subjects were not taken very seriously and on my physics subjects we only had one hour of tutorials each week which is way less than what I'm used to at UCPH. The physics subjects were definitely difficult, but I didn't feel very prepared for the tests and assignments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less contact hours in general. For Physics, we had way less tutorials and lectures. Also, in experience there was a kind of performer culture where students didn't feel very comfortable asking questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took the subjects:
Introduction to Urban Planning
- Interesting subject, has a field trip mid semester - can recommend.
Subatomic Physics
- Interesting subject, bad instruction. Honestly I cannot recommend.
Theoretical Physics 3
- Very good instruction and interesting subject, but be prepared as it is very difficult and you might not want that level of academic stress on exchange.
Language Society and Culture
- Very very nice!! Good and very nice lecturer

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: LSC is nice and maybe TP3 if you want a little challenge.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a very expensive scratch on a rental car :|

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing, and groceries are very expensive here. I really encourage you to make a budget, cause the spending can quickly get out of hand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are so many clubs, and I've heard so many good things about many of them, though I didn't attend them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's free swimming every morning from 9-11, can recommend. They have their own gym also. Theres a bunch of parties directed towards internationals throughout the year, but especially in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The mountaineering club, otherwise just go on a bunch of trips! Use the weekends wisely.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Victoria has so much beautiful nature and with pretty good train access, you can do a lot of hiking trips pretty cost effective. In the mid-semester break, a lot of people go to Tasmania, which I've heard so many good things about. The national parks around are incredible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy enough. It's a former english colony, so it never strays too far from home. It's an incredibly international city, which is very nice. Honestly the academic adjusting was the most difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a share house! Otherwise you can engage in the clubs. It's more difficult to befriend locals but it can definitely be done.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Idk, spiders??

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are so incredibly nice and caring!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Save some money :o
2. Get a share house
3. Try to find subjects that you find interesting but don't require too much exam wise.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bike! It's a pretty bike-friendly city (to international standards), and you can save so much money by getting one. Theres a place called "second-chance bikes" which sells $50 bikes in Collingwood. I can very much recommend that place.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling with incredible people I never would have met otherwise.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from home. It's so far away and expensive, that you can't as easily get visits from friends and family, and the time zone makes it difficult to communicate with the people at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
